category_title: Student with language impairment who shouts out and disrupts others to avoid difficult tasks
minimal_context: James is sitting at his desk in the pull-out special education classroom working on an independent reading worksheet while other students work nearby.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your independent reading worksheet, James. Please complete these questions quietly at your desk.

STUDENT: (Pushes the worksheet away) I'm not doing this. It's too hard.

TUTOR: Just try your best and see what you can do.

STUDENT: (Starts tapping his pencil loudly on the desk and looks away from the paper) I said I'm not doing it!

TUTOR: Please keep your voice down and focus on your own paper.

STUDENT: (Stands up and shouts across the room) HEY! Look at me! This reading is stupid! (Reaches over and grabs the worksheet off the desk of the student sitting next to him)

options.A: Provide the student with access to similar, but more socially appropriate, sensory stimulation by giving him a squishy, stress-relief ball during independent reading worksheets.
options.B: Incorporate basketball references from LeBron James, popular music, or skateboarding references into the independent reading worksheets to engage the student during the activity.
options.C: Create a classroom reading community founded on respect for student choice and individual perspectives to support the student during independent reading worksheet time.
options.D: Provide easy tasks consisting of independent reading worksheets selected by the teacher that the student, without assistance, is likely to complete with 80% or better accuracy.
